title: Reported questions
theme: Reported questions and commands (asked if/whether, asked WH, told to + base, asked to + base)
goal: Student reports yes/no questions, WH-questions, commands, and requests with correct word order (no inversion) and proper structure.
connects_to: M19 (Relative clauses non-defining) — informational expansion in sentences.
module_chunks: He asked if I was tired
She asked whether I had finished
He asked what time it was
She wanted to know how it worked
He told me not to wait
He warned me not to go

units.title: He asked if
units.grammar_focus: Reported yes/no questions (if/whether + statement word order)
units.real_life_context: You report yes/no questions someone asked, without inverting subject and verb.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Are you tired?" Reported: "He asked _____ I was tired."
grammar.explanation: Reported yes/no questions use "if" or "whether". "He asked if I was tired" — no inversion, statement word order.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Do you live here?" Reported: "She asked if I _____ there."
grammar.explanation: Backshift: "do you live" → "lived" (past simple). "Here" → "there". No "do" auxiliary in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Have you finished?" Reported: "He asked if I _____."
grammar.explanation: Present perfect ("have finished") → past perfect ("had finished") in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Will you come?" Reported: "She asked _____ I would come."
grammar.explanation: Yes/no question with "will" → "if + subject + would". "Asked if I would come".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Are you happy?" Reported: "He asked _____ I _____ happy."
grammar.explanation: "If" + statement word order + backshift "are" → "was".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Do you speak English?" Reported: "She asked if I _____ English."
grammar.explanation: "Do you speak" → "spoke" in reported speech (no "do"). Statement structure.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Can you swim?" Reported: "He asked if I _____ swim."
grammar.explanation: Modal "can" → "could" in reported speech. "If I could swim".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Are you tired?" Reported: "He asked if was I tired."
grammar.answer: He asked if I was tired.
grammar.explanation: Classic error: keeping the inversion from the direct question. In reported speech, the order is STATEMENT: "if + subject + verb".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Do you like coffee?" Reported: "She asked if I do like coffee."
grammar.answer: She asked if I liked coffee.
grammar.explanation: Don't use "do" as auxiliary in reported speech (it's no longer a direct question). The direct form converts to the statement form of the verb tense.

grammar.passage: He asked if I was tired. She asked if I lived in São Paulo. He asked if I had finished the report. She asked if I would come to the party. He asked if I could swim.
grammar.question: What did she ask about my home?
grammar.answer: if I lived in São Paulo
grammar.explanation: The text says "She asked if I lived in São Paulo".

listening_speaking.text: He asked if I was tired.
She asked if I lived there.
He asked if I had finished.
She asked if I would come.
He asked if I could swim.

units.title: She asked where
units.grammar_focus: Reported WH-questions (where, what, when, who, why, how — no inversion)
units.real_life_context: You report open-ended questions with WH-words.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Where do you live?" Reported: "He asked _____ I lived."
grammar.explanation: A reported WH-question keeps the WH-word ("where"). No inversion, no "do". "Asked where I lived" — statement word order.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "What time is it?" Reported: "She asked _____."
grammar.explanation: Keep "what time" + statement word order "it was". No verb-subject inversion.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "How do you do it?" Reported: "He asked _____."
grammar.explanation: "How + subject + past simple" with no "do". "How I did it" — statement order in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Why are you late?" Reported: "She asked _____."
grammar.explanation: "Why + I + was" — statement order, with backshift from "are" to "was".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "When will you arrive?" Reported: "He asked when I _____ arrive."
grammar.explanation: "Will" → "would" in reported speech. "When I would arrive".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Who is your boss?" Reported: "She asked who my boss _____."
grammar.explanation: "Is" → "was" in reported speech. "Who my boss was" — statement order.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "What do you want?" Reported: "He asked _____ I wanted."
grammar.explanation: WH-word "what" + statement order. Backshift "want" → "wanted".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Where do you live?" Reported: "He asked where do I live."
grammar.explanation: "Do I live" keeps the question structure. In reported speech, it becomes a statement: "I lived" (no "do").

grammar.sentence: Direct: "What time is it?" Reported: "She asked what time was it."
grammar.answer: She asked what time it was.
grammar.explanation: "Was it" keeps the question inversion. In reported speech, use statement order: "it was".

grammar.passage: He asked where I lived. She asked what time it was. He asked how I did it. She asked why I was late. He asked when I would arrive.
grammar.question: What did he ask about my home?
grammar.explanation: The text says "He asked where I lived".

units.title: He told me to
units.grammar_focus: Reported commands (told + person + to + base / told + person + not to + base)
units.real_life_context: You report orders, instructions, or directives someone gave.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Close the door." Reported: "He told me _____ the door."
grammar.explanation: Reported commands = "told + person + to + base form". "Told me to close the door".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Don't wait for me." Reported: "She told me _____ for her."
grammar.explanation: Negative command: "NOT TO + base". "Told me not to wait" — "not" before "to".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Be quiet." Reported: "He told us _____ quiet."
grammar.explanation: "Told us to be quiet" — to + base form of the verb "be".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Don't speak loudly." Reported: "She told them _____ loudly."
grammar.explanation: Standard negative: "not to + base". "Not to speak loudly".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Open the window." Reported: "He told me _____ the window."
grammar.explanation: "To open" — direct command becomes "to + base".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Don't be late." Reported: "She told me _____ late."
grammar.explanation: Negative command with the verb "be": "not to be late".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Stop running." Reported: "He told the children _____ running."
grammar.explanation: "To stop running" — direct command reported.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Sit down." Reported: "He told me sit down."
grammar.answer: He told me to sit down.
grammar.explanation: Always "told + person + TO + base". "Sit down" without "to" doesn't work in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Don't shout." Reported: "She told me to don't shout."
grammar.answer: She told me not to shout.
grammar.explanation: In reported speech, "don't" disappears. The negative is "NOT TO + base". "To don't shout" doesn't exist.

grammar.passage: He told me to close the door. She told me not to wait. He told us to be quiet. She told them not to speak loudly. He told me to open the window.
grammar.question: What did she tell them not to do?
grammar.explanation: The text says "She told them not to speak loudly".

listening_speaking.text: He told me to close the door.
She told me not to wait.
He told us to be quiet.
She told them not to speak loudly.
He told me to call him later.

units.title: She asked me to
units.grammar_focus: Reported requests (asked + person + to + base) and reporting verbs (asked, begged, urged, warned)
units.real_life_context: You report polite requests, pleas, warnings, and suggestions.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Could you help me?" Reported: "She asked me _____ her."
grammar.explanation: Reported requests: "asked + person + to + base". "Asked me to help her" — the polite request takes a structural command form.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Please don't tell anyone." Reported: "He asked me _____ anyone."
grammar.explanation: Negative request: "asked me not to tell". "Not" before "to".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Please be careful." Reported: "She _____ me to be careful."
grammar.explanation: "Warned + person + to + base" — warning verb. Stronger than "asked".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Please reconsider!" Reported: "He _____ me to reconsider."
grammar.explanation: "Begged + person + to + base" — emotional, pleading request.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Could you wait?" Reported: "She asked me _____ a moment."
grammar.explanation: "To wait" — polite request reported.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Please don't be late." Reported: "He asked me _____ late."
grammar.explanation: Negative request with "be": "not to be late".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Please try harder." Reported: "She _____ me to try harder."
grammar.explanation: "Urged + person + to + base" — emphatic request, encouragement.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Please help me." Reported: "She asked me please to help her."
grammar.answer: She asked me to help her.
grammar.explanation: "Please" doesn't appear in reported speech. "Asked" already implies a polite request. Structure only.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Could you call me?" Reported: "He asked me that I call him."
grammar.answer: He asked me to call him.
grammar.explanation: Requests don't use a "that-clause". Fixed structure: "asked + person + TO + base".

grammar.passage: She asked me to help her. He asked me not to tell anyone. She warned me to be careful. He begged me to reconsider. She urged me to try harder.
grammar.question: What did he beg her to do?
grammar.explanation: The text says "He begged me to reconsider".

listening_speaking.text: She asked me to help her.
He asked me not to tell.
She warned me to be careful.
He begged me to stay.
She urged me to apply.

units.title: Mixed reports
units.grammar_focus: Integration of reported statements, questions, and commands
units.real_life_context: You report complex conversations including statements, questions, and orders fluidly.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I'm tired." Reported: "She said _____ tired."
grammar.explanation: Statement: "said + subject + past tense". "She was tired" — statement word order.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Are you ready?" Reported: "He asked _____ ready."
grammar.explanation: Yes/no question: "if + subject + past tense". "If I was ready" — no inversion.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Close the door." Reported: "She told me _____ the door."
grammar.explanation: Command: "told + person + to + base". "Told me to close the door".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Where do you live?" Reported: "He asked _____ I lived."
grammar.explanation: A reported WH-question keeps the WH-word + statement word order.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Don't be late." Reported: "She told me _____ late."
grammar.explanation: Negative command: "not to + base".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Can you help?" Reported: "He asked _____ I _____ help."
grammar.explanation: "Asked if + subject + could". Backshift "can" → "could".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "I've finished." Reported: "She said she _____ finished."
grammar.explanation: "Have finished" (present perfect) → "had finished" (past perfect) in reported speech.

grammar.sentence: Direct: "What is your name?" Reported: "He asked what is my name."
grammar.answer: He asked what my name was.
grammar.explanation: "Is my name" keeps the inversion. In reported speech, use statement order: "my name was".

grammar.sentence: Direct: "Help me!" Reported: "She told me help her."
grammar.answer: She told me to help her.
grammar.explanation: Reported command: "told + person + TO + base". "Help" without "to" doesn't work.

grammar.question: What did she beg me to do?
grammar.explanation: The text says "She begged me to stay".

She told me to close the door.

cross_unit_consolidation: Reported yes/no: "asked if/whether + subject + past tense"
Reported WH: "asked where/what/when/why/how + subject + past tense" (sem inversão)
Reported command: "told + person + to + base" / "told + person + not to + base"
Reporting verbs variados: asked, told, mentioned, warned, begged, urged, suggested
